title: Expected move grows with the square root of time
summary: Expected move = IV x sqrt(trading days / 252). Trading days are about calendar days x 0.69, because volatility does not accrue over weekends. For a $100 stock with 25% IV and 30 days: 25 x sqrt(30 x 0.69 / 252) is about 7.2%, so two-thirds of the time it stays within about $14.40 centered on today.

params.label: Excess drift over rate
params.help: Your view of annual return above the risk-free rate. Zero = the market view; EV is then about zero.

steps.caption: The distribution of prices 30 days out.
One standard deviation: 25 x sqrt(30 x 0.69 / 252) = about 7.2%, or $92.80 to $107.20.
Two standard deviations: about 14.4%. Doubling time does not double the move.
The move grows with the square root of time: four times the days gives twice the move.

takeaways: Expected move scales with the square root of time, not with time.
Use trading days: calendar days x 0.69, divided by 252.
For one day, IV divided by 16 is a quick estimate.
caveats: The transcript says the range is $14.40 wide, which is plus or minus 7.2% on $100.
